flutter {
    source = "../.."
}

// ── 16 KB page-size gate for prebuilt native assets (gh-746) ─────────────
// flutter_gemma's LiteRT-LM native bundle ships Qualcomm QNN HTP Skel
// libraries whose ELF LOAD segments declare a 4 KB alignment; Google Play
// rejects uploads containing such libraries. The flutter tool stages native
// assets under build/intermediates/flutter/<variant>/native_assets/jniLibs
// during compileFlutterBuild<Variant>, and copyJniLibsflutterBuild<Variant>
// syncs them into the APK afterwards — the patch task runs in between and
// lifts every congruent LOAD segment's p_align to 16 KB (loud failure when a
// future blob needs a real relink instead). Idempotent: already-aligned
===ROOT-GRADLE===
    val newSubprojectBuildDir: Directory = newBuildDir.dir(project.name)
    project.layout.buildDirectory.value(newSubprojectBuildDir)
}

// Pub-resolved plugins (the flutter_js fork pins Kotlin 1.8, flutter_gemma
// pins Java 11) trip AGP 9's "Inconsistent JVM-target compatibility"
// check. Align every plugin subproject to the app's JVM 17 (issue #289):
// the android extension's compileOptions is overridden after each plugin's
// own script ran (afterEvaluate), and the Kotlin compile tasks' jvmTarget
// is set through the task extension/getter so the root script needs no
// Kotlin Gradle Plugin on its classpath.
===MANIFEST===
        <!-- flame_3d (the scene3d GLB path — fitness coach) renders via
             Flutter GPU on Impeller. -->
        <meta-data
            android:name="io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableFlutterGPU"
            android:value="true" />
        <!-- flutter_gemma: required for the GPU backend on Android 12+ — the
             OpenCL loader uses libvndksupport.so (android_load_sphal_library)
             to dlopen the vendor OpenCL driver. Without it OpenCL can't load
             and the engine falls back to WebGPU, which hard-freezes some Mali
             GPUs on the vision encoder (flutter_gemma #324). -->
        <uses-native-library android:name="libvndksupport.so" android:required="false"/>
        <uses-native-library
            android:name="libOpenCL.so"
            android:required="false"/>
        <uses-native-library android:name="libOpenCL-car.so" android:required="false"/>
===PLIST===
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
	<key>CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone</key>
	<true/>
	<!-- flutter_gemma: lets the user browse the downloaded model files in
	     the Files app (recommended by the plugin's iOS setup). -->
	<key>UIFileSharingEnabled</key>
	<true/>
	<key>CFBundleDevelopmentRegion</key>
	<string>$(DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE)</string>
	<key>CFBundleDisplayName</key>
	<string>Fa</string>
	<key>CFBundleExecutable</key>
===ENT===
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
	<!-- flutter_gemma: Gemma 4 weights (2.4–4.3 GB) plus the KV cache exceed
	     the default per-app memory limit on iOS; these entitlements raise it
	     (see the flutter_gemma README's iOS setup section). -->
	<key>com.apple.developer.kernel.extended-virtual-addressing</key>
	<true/>
	<key>com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit</key>
	<true/>
	<!-- fah/health channel: read-only HealthKit access (steps, resting
	     heart rate, sleep) for the health_summary tool + JS bridge. -->
	<key>com.apple.developer.healthkit</key>
	<true/>
	<!-- fah/home channel: HomeKit home control (list homes/rooms/accessories,
	     read/write characteristics, execute scenes). Without this entitlement
	     the access prompt still appears and authorizationStatus reports
	     authorized, but HMHomeManager never delivers homes — listHomes comes
	     back empty forever. Requires the HomeKit capability on the App ID. -->
	<key>com.apple.developer.homekit</key>
	<true/>
	<!-- fah/icloud channel: iCloud Drive ubiquity container (Documents)
	     for syncing sessions/apps across devices. DISABLED until the App ID
	     gets the iCloud capability with container iCloud.dev.fa1.app in
	     the developer portal — without it the release archive fails with
	     "Entitlement ... not found and could not be included in profile".
	     The fah/icloud channel reports unavailable cleanly meanwhile.
	<key>com.apple.developer.icloud-services</key>
	<array>
		<string>CloudDocuments</string>
	</array>
	<key>com.apple.developer.ubiquity-containers</key>
	<array>
		<string>iCloud.dev.fa1.app</string>
	</array>
	-->
</dict>
</plist>

post_install do |installer|
  installer.pods_project.targets.each do |target|
    flutter_additional_macos_build_settings(target)
  end

  # flutter_gemma / LiteRT-LM: copy the Apple companion dylibs into the app
  # bundle as .framework bundles and patch LiteRtLm's load command so that
  # dlopen("LiteRtLm.framework/LiteRtLm") resolves GemmaModelConstraintProvider
  # at runtime. Without this macOS builds crash at first inference.
  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|
    aggregate_target.user_targets.each do |user_target|
      next unless user_target.name == 'Runner'
      phase_name = '[flutter_gemma] Setup LiteRT-LM macOS'
      existing = user_target.shell_script_build_phases.find { |p| p.respond_to?(:name) && p.name == phase_name }
      phase = existing || user_target.new_shell_script_build_phase(phase_name)
      phase.input_paths = [
        '$(BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR)/$(PRODUCT_NAME).app/Contents/Frameworks/LiteRtLm.framework/Versions/A/LiteRtLm',
      ]
      phase.output_paths = ['$(DERIVED_FILE_DIR)/flutter_gemma_litertlm_macos.stamp']
      phase.shell_script = <<~SHELL
        set -e
        FRAMEWORKS="${BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR}/${PRODUCT_NAME}.app/Contents/Frameworks"
        if [ ! -d "${FRAMEWORKS}" ]; then
          exit 0
        fi
        for base in LiteRtMetalAccelerator LiteRtTopKMetalSampler GemmaModelConstraintProvider; do
          rm -f "${FRAMEWORKS}/lib${base}.dylib"
        done
        for candidate in \\
            "${HOME}/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64" \\
            "${PODS_ROOT}/../Flutter/ephemeral/.symlinks/plugins/flutter_gemma/native/litert_lm/prebuilt/macos_arm64" \\
            "${SRCROOT}/../../native/litert_lm/prebuilt/macos_arm64"; do
          if [ -f "${candidate}/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            PLUGIN_PREBUILT="${candidate}"
            break
          fi
        done
        if [ -z "${PLUGIN_PREBUILT:-}" ]; then
          echo "[flutter_gemma] ERROR: Could not find macOS companion dylibs"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "[flutter_gemma] Using companion dylibs from: ${PLUGIN_PREBUILT}"
        for base in GemmaModelConstraintProvider LiteRtMetalAccelerator LiteRtTopKMetalSampler; do
          src="${PLUGIN_PREBUILT}/lib${base}.dylib"
          if [ ! -f "${src}" ]; then
            echo "[flutter_gemma] WARNING: ${src} not found"
            continue
          fi
          fw_dir="${FRAMEWORKS}/${base}.framework"
          mkdir -p "${fw_dir}/Versions/A/Resources"
          cp "${src}" "${fw_dir}/Versions/A/${base}"
          install_name_tool -id "@rpath/${base}.framework/Versions/A/${base}" \\
            "${fw_dir}/Versions/A/${base}" 2>/dev/null || true
          (cd "${fw_dir}" && ln -sfh A Versions/Current && ln -sfh "Versions/Current/${base}" "${base}" && ln -sfh "Versions/Current/Resources" Resources)
          cat > "${fw_dir}/Versions/A/Resources/Info.plist" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

  <key>CFBundlePackageType</key><string>FMWK</string>

  # wasm_run FFI symbols live in a static library inside WasmRun.xcframework.
  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because
  # DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=YES (Release default) still discards the unreferenced
  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive
  # itself so the list stays in sync with the vendored package. Without this
  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen. SRCROOT is the
  # macos/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where vendor/ lives.
  macos_slice = '$(SRCROOT)/../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a'
  macos_archive = File.expand_path('../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a', __dir__)
  ffi_symbols = `nm -gU -arch arm64 #{macos_archive}`.lines
    .map(&:split)
    .select { |cols| %w[T D S].include?(cols[1]) && cols[2] }
    .map { |cols| cols[2] }
    .uniq
    .grep(/^_(wire|new|drop|free|get|store|init|inflate|share)_/)
    .sort

      # Runner script phase that fails on a fresh runner ("Could not find
      # macOS companion dylibs") — seed from the pinned upstream native
      # release, sha256-verified (same incantation as build-macos.yml).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"
          if [ -f "$GEMMA_CACHE/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            echo "companion dylibs already cached"
          else
            echo "seeding companion dylibs from flutter_gemma native-v0.16.0"
            mkdir -p "$GEMMA_CACHE"
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz \
              https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.16.0/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz
            echo "c597554a7a5cdf099658227099a54ef4916c5802b9182757e656e1788f9426b6  /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz -C "$GEMMA_CACHE"
          fi
          ls -la "$GEMMA_CACHE"

      - name: flutter build macos (debug)

          set -o pipefail

- name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # gh-1468: same seed as ci.yml build-android — the release lane runs
      # the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download and rides the same
      # release-asset CDN roulette without it.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # release lane's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the lane. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

===455-465===
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else
            echo "GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      # gh-1468: same seed as the ci.yml/ci AAB jobs — the flavor matrix
      # runs the same flutter_gemma_litertlm hook download per leg.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # flavor matrix's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the leg. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
===1160-1195===
      # #1331 ratchet: per-file uncompressed floor seeded from the last
      # release-shape CI artifact (run 37495702186 fa.ipa) with the diet
      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL fails the leg — same gate
      # family as the macOS pass (#1227). Eviction is pinned separately by
      # the --forbid deny-list: the NEW-line guard alone only catches
      # re-adds above 5% of TOTAL (Symbols/ qualifies at 99 MB; the 5.6 MB
      # glb does not — +3.8% TOTAL, sub-share NEW), so a returning evicted
      # artifact fails via --forbid in the same step. Also pins the owner
      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime and LiteRT LM always ship.
      - name: Size manifest ratchet + wasm keep-set (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          MANIFEST=$(mktemp)
          trap 'rm -f "$MANIFEST"' EXIT
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "$IPA_PATH" \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv \
            --forbid '^Symbols/' --forbid 'coach_anny\.glb$' \
            --manifest-out "$MANIFEST"
          for ASSET in \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/qjs.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/lua.wasm; do
            grep -q "$ASSET" "$MANIFEST" || {
              echo "::error::$ASSET missing from the IPA — the js-apps WASM runtime must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
              exit 1
            }
          done
          grep -q "LiteRtLm.framework/LiteRtLm" "$MANIFEST" || {
            echo "::error::LiteRtLm.framework missing from the IPA — on-device LLM stack must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "✅ wasm runtime + LiteRT keep-set present; iOS size ratchet green"

      - name: Verify IPA and FFI symbols
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"

run: |
          echo "=== Dependency versions ==="
          flutter pub deps --style=compact

      # flutter_gemma ≥1.5.5 no longer downloads the Apple LiteRT-LM companion
      # dylibs from its hook (they are bundled via the Podfile phase), so a
      # fresh runner has nothing at ~/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma and the
      # Runner script phase fails with "Could not find macOS companion
      # dylibs". Seed the cache from the upstream native release (pinned,
      # sha256-verified).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"
          if [ -f "$GEMMA_CACHE/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            echo "companion dylibs already cached"
          else
            echo "seeding companion dylibs from flutter_gemma native-v0.16.0"
            mkdir -p "$GEMMA_CACHE"
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56);
            # --retry-all-errors retries them (sha256 below guards corruption)
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz \
              https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.16.0/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz

ok

      - uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # gh-1468: pre-seed the flutter_gemma LiteRT-LM Android cache on the
      # android matrix row (no-op elsewhere) — same release-asset CDN
      # roulette as the PR leg, same fix.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed
        if: matrix.target == 'android'

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android, on the
      # android matrix row only (no-op elsewhere) — Gradle configuration

      # The macOS Podfile bundles the LiteRT-LM companion dylibs via a
      # Runner script phase that fails on a fresh runner ("Could not find
      # macOS companion dylibs") — seed from the pinned upstream native
      # release, sha256-verified (same incantation as build-macos.yml).
      - name: Ensure flutter_gemma macOS companion dylibs
        if: matrix.target == 'macos'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GEMMA_CACHE="$HOME/Library/Caches/flutter_gemma/native/macos_arm64"
          if [ -f "$GEMMA_CACHE/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib" ]; then
            echo "companion dylibs already cached"
          else
            echo "seeding companion dylibs from flutter_gemma native-v0.16.0"
            mkdir -p "$GEMMA_CACHE"
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz \
              https://github.com/DenisovAV/flutter_gemma/releases/download/native-v0.16.0/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz
            echo "c597554a7a5cdf099658227099a54ef4916c5802b9182757e656e1788f9426b6  /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz" | shasum -a 256 -c -
            tar xzf /tmp/litertlm-macos_arm64.tar.gz -C "$GEMMA_CACHE"
          fi
          ls -la "$GEMMA_CACHE"

      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

# gh-2004: [GOAL] Remove on-device Gemma stack: flutter_gemma + litertlm packages, lib/gemma/ + lib/on_device/ modules, model-cache/settings UI, pod plumbing (iOS 16 floor note) — zero dead code, graceful config migration, all platforms green

## Description

**[WIP][GOAL] Remove the on-device Gemma stack from the app entirely: `flutter_gemma` + `flutter_gemma_litertlm` + LiteRT/MediaPipe dependency tree, the `lib/gemma/` module, on-device wiring/settings/model-cache UI, platform pod plumbing — zero dead code, graceful migration of persisted configs, all platforms build green**

Owner directive (2026-10-30): «убрать local LLMs flutter gemma (как она у нас называется) и все её зависимости». Clarification: **no migration** — just drop local models and cache if present; if a gemma model was installed/selected, silently reset to the default.

## Goal
One sentence: **after this card the app has NO on-device Gemma/LiteRT inference anywhere — no packages, no module code, no settings/cache UI, no pod/gradle plumbing, no orphaned configs — and cloud-connection behavior is byte-identical to today.**

## Inventory (verified on the working tree, ~39 files touched)
- **Packages** (`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:152-161`): `flutter_gemma: ^1.5.2`, `flutter_gemma_litertlm: ^1.3.1`, plus the explicitly pinned transitive web pins for the litertlm/`@litert-lm/core` path.
- **Module** `lib/gemma/` (9 files): `gemma_service.dart` (+plugin/stub), `gemma_stream_function.dart`, `gemma_types.dart`, `gemma_cache_section.dart`, `gemma_web_registration*` (web/dart/stub).
- **On-device plumbing** `lib/on_device/`: `on_device_stream_pump.dart`, `on_device_message_codec.dart`; `lib/services/ondevice_config_store.dart`; touchpoints in `agent_service*.dart` (wiring/compaction/media/host_builder/connection_guard), `last_connection.dart`, `quota_store.dart`, `analytics.dart`, `boot/app_boot.dart`, `boot/boot_config_codec.dart`, `main.dart`, `prompts.g.dart`.
- **UI**: `models_settings_page.dart`, `settings_flows.dart`, `providers_section.dart`, `settings.dart`, `model_cache_section.dart`, `provider_selection_list.dart`, `downloaded_models_quick_start.dart`; l10n strings (en/ru + generated).
- **Platform plumbing**: `ios/Podfile` + lock (iOS 16 floor comment «required by flutter_gamma», static linking for LiteRT-LM frameworks), `macos/Podfile` + lock (companion dylibs copy step), Android gradle if present, web registration hooks.

## Capability surface / removal contract
| Piece | Contract |
|---|---|
| Packages | both gemma packages + their explicit pins removed; `flutter pub deps` shows no gemma/litert/mediapipe transitive residue |
| Module code | `lib/gemma/` and `lib/on_device/` deleted wholesale; every import site cleaned — grep gate `gemma|litert|litertlm|mediapipe` over `lib/` returns ZERO (case-insensitive) |
| Settings UI | models-settings page section, provider list on-device entries, model-cache/downloaded-models UI, quick-start card removed; `/settings` hub reflows without dead links; l10n strings deleted (not commented out) |
| Wiring | AgentService/compaction/media/host_builder/connection_guard on-device branches removed; cloud relay path byte-identical (REG: agent_service suites green untouched) |
| Persisted configs | **NO migration.** boot/last_connection/ondevice stores carrying gemma entries are simply RESET to the default cloud connection on load — silently, no notice, no migration logic; codecs keep tolerant-parse of old bytes (unknown/dropped fields skipped, never a crash) |
| Downloaded model files | **DROPPED outright:** on first boot the new build deletes cached `.litertlm`/model artifacts (best-effort; delete failure is non-fatal and logged once). No settings action, no prompts |
| Platform floors | iOS 16 floor was raised FOR flutter_gemma (`ios/Podfile:2`): evaluate reverting to the pre-gemma floor as a FOLLOW-UP commit (other code may now require 16 — do not blind-revert); macOS dylib copy step removed |
| Analytics/quota | on-device usage counters/references removed; analytics schema unchanged for cloud events |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `grep -ri 'gemma\|litert\|litertlm\|mediapipe' flutter_app/lib flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` → zero hits (case-insensitive, generated files included); `flutter pub deps` — no gemma/litert/mediapipe packages.
- **AC2** — Each platform builds: iOS, macOS, Android, web (the web registration path removal included) — build jobs green; crap/LOC gates green (`crap4dart.yaml` app gate stays within baseline).
- **AC3** — REG: all cloud-connection suites green byte-identically (relay, compaction, media, quota); red REG blocks merge.
- **AC4** — Drop IT: a pre-removal boot config + ondevice store fixture (gemma connection selected) loads on the new build → resets to the default cloud connection SILENTLY (no notice, no migration code path), no crash; cached-model fixture dir → files deleted on first boot (best-effort).
- **AC5** — Settings UI shows no on-device/gemma entries, no dead navigation targets; l10n compile clean (en/ru).
- **AC6** — Cached-model cleanup path: fixture cache dir → settings/first-boot action deletes files; skip path leaves no functional trace.
- **AC7** — Grep gate wired into the app quality gate as a REG (a future gemma re-introduction needs a deliberate new card, not an accident).

## Edge / border cases
User mid-session on a gemma connection at upgrade time → next connection resolves to the cloud default (silent reset); scheduled/headless runs referencing a gemma provider id (same reset path); `prompts.g.dart` regeneration (no stale prompt references); store codecs keep tolerant parse of OLD bytes (skipped fields, no version hard-cut); cache-delete on a read-only volume → logged once, ignored.

## Non-goals
WebLLM and transformers_js web engines are SEPARATE local-model stacks — NOT touched by this card unless a follow-up owner directive says otherwise; cloud `inspect_image`/`transcribe_audio` slots untouched; no replacement on-device inference in this card.

## References
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:152-161`, `lib/gemma/*`, `lib/on_device/*`, `ios/Podfile:2,32,147`, `macos/Podfile:43`, file inventory above; removal follows the repo's standard: TDD-friendly grep gates + platform build greens.

One sentence: **after this card the app has NO on-device Gemma/LiteRT inference anywhere — no packages, no module code, no settings/cache UI, no pod/gradle plumbing, no orphaned configs — and cloud-connection behavior is byte-identical to today.**

## Capability surface / removal contract
| Piece | Contract |
|---|---|
| Packages | both gemma packages + their explicit pins removed; `flutter pub deps` shows no gemma/litert/mediapipe transitive residue |
| Module code | `lib/gemma/` and `lib/on_device/` deleted wholesale; every import site cleaned — grep gate `gemma|litert|litertlm|mediapipe` over `lib/` returns ZERO (case-insensitive) |
| Settings UI | models-settings page section, provider list on-device entries, model-cache/downloaded-models UI, quick-start card removed; `/settings` hub reflows without dead links; l10n strings deleted (not commented out) |
| Wiring | AgentService/compaction/media/host_builder/connection_guard on-device branches removed; cloud relay path byte-identical (REG: agent_service suites green untouched) |
| Persisted configs | **NO migration.** boot/last_connection/ondevice stores carrying gemma entries are simply RESET to the default cloud connection on load — silently, no notice, no migration logic; codecs keep tolerant-parse of old bytes (unknown/dropped fields skipped, never a crash) |
| Downloaded model files | **DROPPED outright:** on first boot the new build deletes cached `.litertlm`/model artifacts (best-effort; delete failure is non-fatal and logged once). No settings action, no prompts |
| Platform floors | iOS 16 floor was raised FOR flutter_gemma (`ios/Podfile:2`): evaluate reverting to the pre-gemma floor as a FOLLOW-UP commit (other code may now require 16 — do not blind-revert); macOS dylib copy step removed |
| Analytics/quota | on-device usage counters/references removed; analytics schema unchanged for cloud events |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `grep -ri 'gemma\|litert\|litertlm\|mediapipe' flutter_app/lib flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` → zero hits (case-insensitive, generated files included); `flutter pub deps` — no gemma/litert/mediapipe packages.
- **AC2** — Each platform builds: iOS, macOS, Android, web (the web registration path removal included) — build jobs green; crap/LOC gates green (`crap4dart.yaml` app gate stays within baseline).
- **AC3** — REG: all cloud-connection suites green byte-identically (relay, compaction, media, quota); red REG blocks merge.
- **AC4** — Drop IT: a pre-removal boot config + ondevice store fixture (gemma connection selected) loads on the new build → resets to the default cloud connection SILENTLY (no notice, no migration code path), no crash; cached-model fixture dir → files deleted on first boot (best-effort).
- **AC5** — Settings UI shows no on-device/gemma entries, no dead navigation targets; l10n compile clean (en/ru).
- **AC6** — Cached-model cleanup path: fixture cache dir → settings/first-boot action deletes files; skip path leaves no functional trace.
- **AC7** — Grep gate wired into the app quality gate as a REG (a future gemma re-introduction needs a deliberate new card, not an accident).

## Edge / border cases
User mid-session on a gemma connection at upgrade time → next connection resolves to the cloud default (silent reset); scheduled/headless runs referencing a gemma provider id (same reset path); `prompts.g.dart` regeneration (no stale prompt references); store codecs keep tolerant parse of OLD bytes (skipped fields, no version hard-cut); cache-delete on a read-only volume → logged once, ignored.

## Non-goals
WebLLM and transformers_js web engines are SEPARATE local-model stacks — NOT touched by this card unless a follow-up owner directive says otherwise; cloud `inspect_image`/`transcribe_audio` slots untouched; no replacement on-device inference in this card.

reasoning as webllm_helpers.js). -->
  <script src="transformers_js_helpers.js"></script>
  <!-- WebLLM (@mlc-ai/web-llm, pinned): runs small LLMs on-device via WebGPU.
       Loaded as an ES module from jsdelivr and exposed as window.webllm for
       the Dart side (lib/webllm/). Version matches the interop bindings.
       Used chat-only: tool calling is the Dart-side prompt-tools wrapper's
       job, not the engine's native function-calling mode. -->
  <script type="module" src="inline_script_4.js"></script>
  <!-- Transformers.js (@huggingface/transformers, pinned): runs Gemma 4 ONNX
       on-device via ONNX Runtime Web + WebGPU — the web on-device Gemma path
       (lib/transformers_js/), replacing the litert-lm web engine below.
       v3.x has no Gemma 4 support, so this pins 4.2.0 (the version family
       the webml-community/Gemma-4-WebGPU space runs). Loaded as an ES module
       from jsdelivr and exposed as window.transformersjs for the Dart side;
       onnxruntime-web's WASM/WebGPU assets load from jsdelivr automatically.
       Weights download from huggingface.co into CacheStorage on first use. -->
  <script type="module" src="inline_script_5.js"></script>
  <!-- LiteRT-LM web engine, formerly used by the on-device Gemma provider.
       DEAD on web since the transformers.js provider above replaced it (the
       pinned @litert-lm/core 0.12.1 crashes creating the GPU executor for
       the -web.litertlm builds, and newer engines break the flutter_gemma
       web streaming pump) — kept only because removal touches the plugin's
       awaited window.litertLmReady handshake; cleanup is tracked as
       follow-up work. Mobile builds still use flutter_gemma via FFI. -->
  <script type="module" src="inline_script_6.js"></script>
  <!-- flutter_gemma web storage helpers. opfs_helper.js (defines
       window.flutterGemmaOPFS) is required by WebStorageMode.streaming —
       Gemma 4 E2B/E4B exceed Chrome's ~2 GB single-blob limit, so the model
       streams into OPFS and the engine consumes a ReadableStream. The pub
       package does not ship opfs_helper.js; it is vendored here from the
       flutter_gemma repo (interface matches flutter_gemma 1.3.1's
       web_opfs_interop.dart). cache_api.js ships inside the pub package and
       backs the non-streaming fallback paths. -->
  <script src="fs_store.js"></script>
  <script src="cache_api.js"></script>
  <script src="opfs_helper.js"></script>
  <script src="flutter_bootstrap.js" async></script>

- name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: this leg runs on ubuntu
      # and the baselines are macOS-captured. Goldens are guarded by the
      # pinned-font leg in the nightly build-release macOS row (issue
      # #1856): the test env renders every glyph from bundled fonts, so a
      # golden diff fails the same way on any host (#177 E5/OQ3).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (macOS-captured baselines, see the golden
        # comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      # gh-1724 review follow-up: same gh-1412 one-shot retry as the other
      # sharded evidence legs — app-crap-gate hard-fails its merge on
      # `count != 2`, so one transient blob-storage finalize error must

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Golden-test gate for flutter_app.

Verifies that golden (screenshot) tests exist and are up to date:

  1. test/golden/goldens/ holds generated snapshots (*.png);
  2. every committed snapshot is still REFERENCED by a golden test
     (orphan check — deleted widgets/tests must not leave stale PNGs
     rotting in the repo and in git history);
  3. every lib/ widget file has golden coverage (enforced by
     test/golden/golden_guard_test.dart — this script runs it plus the
     golden suite, unless --quick is passed, in which case only the
     snapshot-existence and orphan checks run).

Usage:
  python3 scripts/check_goldens.py           # full: run the golden suite
  python3 scripts/check_goldens.py --quick   # existence + orphan checks only

Regenerate snapshots after intentional UI changes:
  cd flutter_app && flutter test test/golden --update-goldens
…then REVIEW every changed PNG before committing.
"""

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
APP_DIR = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "flutter_app")
GOLDENS_DIR = os.path.join(APP_DIR, "test", "golden", "goldens")
GUARD_TEST = os.path.join(APP_DIR, "test", "golden", "golden_guard_test.dart")
GOLDEN_TESTS_DIR = os.path.join(APP_DIR, "test", "golden")
# Committed PTY reference fixtures (issue #810, S7): the omp reference
# captures are the ONLY tracked files under the PTY screenshots dir (the
# runtime screenshot outputs are gitignored, issue #860) — the orphan guard
# covers them so a renamed/dropped scenario never leaves dead PNGs/TXTs.
PTY_SHOTS_DIR = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "test", "integration", "screenshots")
PTY_SOURCE_DIRS = [
    GOLDEN_TESTS_DIR,
    os.path.join(APP_DIR, "test", "cli_visual"),
    os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "test", "cli"),
]

# Single-line quoted string literal carrying an interpolation (multi-line
# scanning would mispair on apostrophes inside comments; golden names are
# always single-line).
_STRING_LITERAL = re.compile(r"'([^'\n]*\$[^'\n]*)'|\"([^\"\n]*\$[^\"\n]*)\"")
# Dart interpolation inside a literal: $identifier or ${expression}.
_INTERPOLATION = re.compile(r"\$[A-Za-z_]\w*|\$\{[^}]*\}")


def golden_name_patterns(sources: str) -> list[re.Pattern[str]]:
    """Regexes for golden names built by string interpolation.

    Tests compose snapshot names like 'chat_header_${width.round()}' or
    'chat_bubble_1_image_$suffix' — a verbatim substring search can never
    see the generated PNG stems, so interpolated literals become regexes
    with each interpolation matching any non-quote run.
    """
    patterns = []
    for match in _STRING_LITERAL.finditer(sources):
        literal = match.group(1) if match.group(1) is not None else match.group(2)
        # A pure-interpolation literal ('$suffix') would degrade to a
        # match-everything pattern and whitelist every root-level golden
        # stem — skip literals without a usable literal anchor.
        if len(_INTERPOLATION.sub("", literal).strip()) < 3:
            continue
        # Substitute BEFORE escaping so re.escape does not mangle the $.
        regex = re.escape(_INTERPOLATION.sub("\x00", literal)).replace(
            "\x00", "[^'/]+"
        )
        patterns.append(re.compile(f"^{regex}$"))
    return patterns


def fail(msg: str) -> int:
    print(f"ERROR: {msg}")
    print()
    print("Golden tests keep the UI pixel-stable. To fix:")
    print("  1. Write/extend tests in flutter_app/test/golden/ (see")
    print("     golden_test_helper.dart) for every widget you added or changed.")
    print("  2. Regenerate snapshots:")
    print("     cd flutter_app && flutter test test/golden --update-goldens")
    print("  3. Review every changed/added PNG, then rerun this script.")
    return 1

def check(artifact: Path, baseline_path: Path, budget_pct: float,
          init_if_missing: bool = False, reseed: bool = False,
          manifest_out=None, forbid=None, vendored=None,
          strict_vendored=False) -> int:
    manifest = build_manifest(artifact, MIN_BYTES)
    if manifest_out:
        write_baseline(manifest_out, manifest)

    # Deny-list (gh-1331 review): a returning evicted artifact fails the
    # gate in every mode — budget and NEW-line share both miss sub-5%
    # re-adds, so eviction is pinned by pattern, not by the floor.
    forbid_res = [re.compile(p) for p in forbid or []]
    if forbid_res:
        banned = [name for name in sorted(manifest)
                  if name != "TOTAL" and any(r.search(name) for r in forbid_res)]
        if banned:
            for name in banned:
                print(f"::error::size_manifest: FORBIDDEN row in {artifact}: "
                      f"{name} ({manifest[name]} bytes) — matches --forbid; "
                      "the artifact was evicted and must not return")
            return 1

    if not baseline_path.exists():
        if init_if_missing:
            write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
            print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline initialized from this "
                  f"artifact — COMMIT {baseline_path} to arm the gate")
            print(fmt_table(manifest))
            return 0
        print(f"::error::size_manifest: baseline {baseline_path} missing "
              f"(run with --init-if-missing to seed it)")
        return 2

    if reseed:
        write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
        print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline RESEEDED from this "
              f"artifact — {baseline_path} rewritten; COMMIT it to make "
              f"the new shape the floor")
        print(fmt_table(manifest))
        return 0

    baseline = load_baseline(baseline_path)
    base_total = baseline["TOTAL"]
    failures, vendored_failures = [], []
    grew, shrank, new, removed = [], [], [], []

    # Vendored carve-out (#1431): engine/vendor rows breach with a
    # ::warning and never redden the job; the budget's TOTAL compares the
    # first-party aggregate only. --strict-vendored gives the teeth back.
    vendored_res = ([] if strict_vendored
                    else [re.compile(p) for p in VENDORED_DEFAULTS + list(vendored or [])])

    def is_vendored(name: str) -> bool:
        return any(r.search(name) for r in vendored_res)

    def fp_total(manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> int:
        return manifest["TOTAL"] - sum(n for k, n in manifest.items()
                                       if k != "TOTAL" and is_vendored(k))

size_manifest semantics: `removed` baseline rows are NOT failures (only reported as improvements). Missing gema frameworks in a new build → rows land in `removed` → gate stays green, prints "removed". So the TSV baselines DON'T need editing for correctness — stale rows are benign (they just report removal).

BUT: keeping dead floor rows is untidy; and the ticket's "zero dead code" spirit — the floors exist to prevent REGROWTH; a gema framework row's floor would silently allow re-adding up to +5%... but --forbid is the eviction pin. For iOS the keep-set grep I already removed from build-mobile.yml. For tidiness AND correctness of "must not return", the right tool is --forbid patterns, which the iOS gate already has for Symbols/ and the glb. Adding `--forbid 'GemmaModelConstraintProvider' --forbid 'LiteRtLm'` etc. would pin eviction... but careful: LiteRtMetalAccelerator — is that gema-only or used by other LiteRT components? With the whole gema stack gone, all three frameworks go.

Decision: update the three TSVs (ios, macos) to drop the gema framework rows (they're dead floors), AND add --forbid pins in build-mobile.yml iOS gate so a re-introduction fails hard. Wait — fa-macos-arm64.tsv: used by build-macos.yml's size gate — check how it's invoked there and whether a keep-set grep exists for macos too (I remember seeing one?). Earlier I only removed the LiteRtLm grep from build-mobile (iOS). Check build-macos.yml for GemaModelConstraintProvider/LiteRtLm greps.

Hmm — but should I even touch the TSVs? "removed" rows are benign... but gh-1684 precedent: baselines get reseed when the artifact SHAPE changes intentionally. The gate philosophy: baseline = floor of the current release shape. Stale rows for removed artifacts → future grows of OTHER files compare against old TOTAL (fine, TOTAL only counts first-party growth... actually base_fp includes removed gema bytes → new TOTAL% change is LOWER (dropped bytes offset growth) → gate more lenient than reality. Minor.

Given AC "no orphaned configs / zero dead code", I'll remove the rows + add --forbid pins for the gema frameworks on the iOS gate, and check the macOS gate invocation.

Also: fixture in test/ci_1820 test mirrors the TSV rows (fixture = the manifest of the OLD artifact) — that's test data for the parser; if I edit the TSV, the test fixture is independent (it tests the parser on a past manifest). import subprocess, struct, zlib
# minimal PNG decode via zlib + reconstruct
def read_png(path):
    data = open(path,'rb').read()
    pos = 8; w=h=None; idat=b''; plte=None; trns=None
    ctype=None; bd=None
    while pos < len(data):
        ln = struct.unpack('>I', data[pos:pos+4])[0]
        typ = data[pos+4:pos+8]
        chunk = data[pos+8:pos+8+ln]
        if typ==b'IHDR':
            w,h,bd,ctype = struct.unpack('>IIBB', chunk[:10])
        elif typ==b'IDAT': idat += chunk
        elif typ==b'PLTE': plte = chunk
        pos += 12+ln
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    ch = {0:1,2:3,3:1,4:2,6:4}[ctype]
    stride = w*ch
    out = bytearray(w*h*ch)
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    pos=0
    for y in range(h):
        f = raw[pos]; pos+=1
        line = bytearray(raw[pos:pos+stride]); pos+=stride
        if f==1:
            for i in range(ch,stride): line[i]=(line[i]+line[i-ch])&255
        elif f==2:
            for i in range(stride): line[i]=(line[i]+prev[i])&255
        elif f==3:
            for i in range(stride):
                a = line[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                line[i]=(line[i]+((a+prev[i])>>1))&255
        elif f==4:
            for i in range(stride):
                a = line[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                b = prev[i]
                c = prev[i-ch] if i>=ch else 0
                p=a+b-c; pa=abs(p-a); pb=abs(p-b); pc=abs(p-c)
                pr = a if (pa<=pb and pa<=pc) else (b if pb<=pc else c)
                line[i]=(line[i]+pr)&255
        out[y*stride:(y+1)*stride]=line
        prev=line
    return w,h,ch,bytes(out)

pr_base_branch.txt
{
  "key": "gh-2004",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Remove on-device Gemma stack: flutter_gemma + litertlm packages, lib/gemma/ + lib/on_device/ modules, model-cache/settings UI, pod plumbing (iOS 16 floor note) — zero dead code, graceful config migration, all platforms green",
    "description": "**[WIP][GOAL] Remove the on-device Gemma stack from the app entirely: `flutter_gemma` + `flutter_gemma_litertlm` + LiteRT/MediaPipe dependency tree, the `lib/gemma/` module, on-device wiring/settings/model-cache UI, platform pod plumbing — zero dead code, graceful migration of persisted configs, all platforms build green**

Owner directive (2026-10-30): «убрать local LLMs flutter gemma (как она у нас называется) и все её зависимости». Clarification: **no migration** — just drop local models and cache if present; if a gemma model was installed/selected, silently reset to the default.

## Goal
One sentence: **after this card the app has NO on-device Gemma/LiteRT inference anywhere — no packages, no module code, no settings/cache UI, no pod/gradle plumbing, no orphaned configs — and cloud-connection behavior is byte-identical to today.**

## Inventory (verified on the working tree, ~39 files touched)
- **Packages** (`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:152-161`): `flutter_gemma: ^1.5.2`, `flutter_gemma_litertlm: ^1.3.1`, plus the explicitly pinned transitive web pins for the litertlm/`@litert-lm/core` path.
- **Module** `lib/gemma/` (9 files): `gemma_service.dart` (+plugin/stub), `gemma_stream_function.dart`, `gemma_types.dart`, `gemma_cache_section.dart`, `gemma_web_registration*` (web/dart/stub).
- **On-device plumbing** `lib/on_device/`: `on_device_stream_pump.dart`, `on_device_message_codec.dart`; `lib/services/ondevice_config_store.dart`; touchpoints in `agent_service*.dart` (wiring/compaction/media/host_builder/connection_guard), `last_connection.dart`, `quota_store.dart`, `analytics.dart`, `boot/app_boot.dart`, `boot/boot_config_codec.dart`, `main.dart`, `prompts.g.dart`.
- **UI**: `models_settings_page.dart`, `settings_flows.dart`, `providers_section.dart`, `settings.dart`, `model_cache_section.dart`, `provider_selection_list.dart`, `downloaded_models_quick_start.dart`; l10n strings (en/ru + generated).
- **Platform plumbing**: `ios/Podfile` + lock (iOS 16 floor comment «required by flutter_gamma», static linking for LiteRT-LM frameworks), `macos/Podfile` + lock (companion dylibs copy step), Android gradle if present, web registration hooks.

## Capability surface / removal contract
| Piece | Contract |
|---|---|
| Packages | both gemma packages + their explicit pins removed; `flutter pub deps` shows no gemma/litert/mediapipe transitive residue |
| Module code | `lib/gemma/` and `lib/on_device/` deleted wholesale; every import site cleaned — grep gate `gemma|litert|litertlm|mediapipe` over `lib/` returns ZERO (case-insensitive) |
| Settings UI | models-settings page section, provider list on-device entries, model-cache/downloaded-models UI, quick-start card removed; `/settings` hub reflows without dead links; l10n strings deleted (not commented out) |
| Wiring | AgentService/compaction/media/host_builder/connection_guard on-device branches removed; cloud relay path byte-identical (REG: agent_service suites green untouched) |
| Persisted configs | **NO migration.** boot/last_connection/ondevice stores carrying gemma entries are simply RESET to the default cloud connection on load — silently, no notice, no migration logic; codecs keep tolerant-parse of old bytes (unknown/dropped fields skipped, never a crash) |
| Downloaded model files | **DROPPED outright:** on first boot the new build deletes cached `.litertlm`/model artifacts (best-effort; delete failure is non-fatal and logged once). No settings action, no prompts |
| Platform floors | iOS 16 floor was raised FOR flutter_gemma (`ios/Podfile:2`): evaluate reverting to the pre-gemma floor as a FOLLOW-UP commit (other code may now require 16 — do not blind-revert); macOS dylib copy step removed |
| Analytics/quota | on-device usage counters/references removed; analytics schema unchanged for cloud events |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — `grep -ri 'gemma\|litert\|litertlm\|mediapipe' flutter_app/lib flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` → zero hits (case-insensitive, generated files included); `flutter pub deps` — no gemma/litert/mediapipe packages.
- **AC2** — Each platform builds: iOS, macOS, Android, web (the web registration path removal included) — build jobs green; crap/LOC gates green (`crap4dart.yaml` app gate stays within baseline).
- **AC3** — REG: all cloud-connection suites green byte-identically (relay, compaction, media, quota); red REG blocks merge.
- **AC4** — Drop IT: a pre-removal boot config + ondevice store fixture (gemma connection selected) loads on the new build → resets to the default cloud connection SILENTLY (no notice, no migration code path), no crash; cached-model fixture dir → files deleted on first boot (best-effort).
- **AC5** — Settings UI shows no on-device/gemma entries, no dead navigation targets; l10n compile clean (en/ru).
- **AC6** — Cached-model cleanup path: fixture cache dir → settings/first-boot action deletes files; skip path leaves no functional trace.
- **AC7** — Grep gate wired into the app quality gate as a REG (a future gemma re-introduction needs a deliberate new card, not an accident).

## Edge / border cases
User mid-session on a gemma connection at upgrade time → next connection resolves to the cloud default (silent reset); scheduled/headless runs referencing a gemma provider id (same reset path); `prompts.g.dart` regeneration (no stale prompt references); store codecs keep tolerant parse of OLD bytes (skipped fields, no version hard-cut); cache-delete on a read-only volume → logged once, ignored.

## Non-goals
WebLLM and transformers_js web engines are SEPARATE local-model stacks — NOT touched by this card unless a follow-up owner directive says otherwise; cloud `inspect_image`/`transcribe_audio` slots untouched; no replacement on-device inference in this card.

## References
`flutter_app/pubspec.yaml:152-161`, `lib/gemma/*`, `lib/on_device/*`, `ios/Podfile:2,32,147`, `macos/Podfile:43`, file inventory above; removal follows the repo's standard: TDD-friendly grep gates + platform build greens."

arguments.content:
### What changed

Removed the on-device Gemma stack end-to-end: `flutter_gemma` + `flutter_gemma_litertlm` packages and their pinned web transitive deps, `lib/gemma/` (9 files), gema wiring in `agent_service*`/`last_connection`/`quota_store`/`analytics`/`boot`, settings/model-cache/quick-start UI and l10n strings (en/ru), pod plumbing (iOS/macOS), web helpers (`inline_script_6.js`, `cache_api.js`, `opfs_helper.js`), and the CI seed/dylib steps (`.github/actions/flutter-gemma-android-seed`, macOS companion-dylib seeding, iOS `LiteRtLm` keep-set grep). Net: 117 files, −6.5k/+0.8k lines.

### Key decisions

- **No migration, silent reset** — persisted `boot`/`last_connection`/on-device stores carrying a `gemma` kind reset to the default cloud connection on load (`last_connection.dart`, `ondevice_config_store.dart` keep tolerant old-bytes parse; `markConfigured('gemma')` now refuses).
- **First-boot artifact drop** — new `lib/services/leftover_model_cleanup.dart` (+ `web_model_artifacts*` OPFS seam) deletes cached `.litertlm`/model files on boot; delete failure is recorded once, never fatal (IO walk + web-store paths unit-tested).
- **`lib/on_device/` stays** — the ticket listed it for deletion, but it is now the shared pump/codec skeleton of the surviving WebLLM + transformers.js engines (verified: both stream functions import it).
- **AC1 raw grep residue is intentional** — the non-goal stacks (`transformers_js`, `webllm` catalogs), the removal machinery, and the two reset codecs are the only remaining token hits; `test/gemma_removal_gate_test.dart` (AC7 REG) encodes exactly this allowlist and makes any other `gemma|litert|litertlm|mediapipe` hit under `flutter_app/lib` or `pubspec.yaml` red.
- **Goldens not re-baked here** — baselines are captured on the pinned macOS runner (`flutter 3.47.4`, per `#1856`); this host cannot reproduce them even for unchanged screens (verified: base `setup_first_run_phone.png` fails locally on the pinned SDK). Baselines were restored byte-for-byte; the 3 gema-affected goldens (`sections_cache_settings`, `setup_quick_start_desktop/phone`) need the documented `flutter test test/golden --update-goldens` re-bake on the release runner. `sections_quick_start.png` was deleted with its widget (orphan gate green).
- iOS 16 floor kept (per ticket: no blind revert; follow-up card evaluates lowering).

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app
flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings   # 0 errors
```

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
2.6. **Conformance coverage** — applies ONLY when the final claim includes behavioral conformance: "matches the reference/specification", parity with an existing implementation, protocol/format compliance — any domain. Happy-path agreement certifies nothing about rejection paths or option combinations: two implementations agreeing on every well-formed input can still diverge exactly where one of them must say no. A conformance item counts as verified only when the checklist also quotes **negative and combination checks**, each one actually run and quoted in its ledger row: inputs that must be rejected or must error, combinations of incompatible/mutually exclusive options that must be refused, empty and corrupt inputs, boundary values, "must NOT work" / "must not find" cases — alongside the happy paths. A blanket "everything matches" without such coverage is not verified: mark the item `fail` and run the missing cases.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.
